key_insight: OctoSense introduces a rich open-source multimodal robot sensing platform and dataset designed to make self-supervised learning more robust in real-world, sensor-degraded conditions. It combines many synchronized sensor streams so models can learn useful representations without requiring manual labels.
problem_solved: Robotic perception systems often fail when one or more sensors are noisy, missing, or degraded, and collecting labeled multimodal robot data is expensive. This paper addresses the need for large-scale, time-synchronized, multi-sensor data that supports self-supervised learning across challenging environments.
method: Builds an open-source sensor platform with stereo RGB, event cameras, LiDAR, thermal imaging, IMU, RTK-corrected GPS, and proprioception data.
Collects 59 hours of synchronized driving data across diverse environments, times of day, and degraded sensor conditions.
Uses the dataset to demonstrate multimodal self-supervised learning for robot perception.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, OctoSense offers a realistic benchmark for learning robust multimodal representations in robotics. It can help improve perception systems that continue working when sensors become unreliable or partially unavailable.

paper_title: OctoSense: Self-Supervised Learning for Multimodal Robot Perception
paper_authors: Anthony Bisulco, Jeremy Wang, Kostas Daniilidis, Randall Balestriero, Pratik Chaudhari
